text:
incident-bot: Paging SRE oncall — multigpu serving cluster reporting recurring NCCL TIMEOUTs and container Xid 79 errors, p95 generation latency > 10s for some customers

sre_alex: seeing repeated logs: "NCCL WARN Call to MPI_Recv timed out" and CUDA error Xid 79 around the same time, GPUs on node gpu-node-12 flapping

eli: stack traces attached in ops: `nccl_socket.c:1423` and `collective_manager.cpp:88` — looks like communicator reset during rendezvous

maggie: customer impact: three customers reported 502s from hosted API routes, capacity autoscale tried to spin up but containers got OOMKilled mid-start

eli: kv-cache eviction spike observed prior to failures, sequence length for several jobs jumped to ~2048, pushing memory usage up

dev-platform: checking kube events — saw `OOMKilled` + `NodeNotReady` events on gpu-node-12 at 15:02:10 UTC, kubelet report: docker/CRIO restarted containerd

sre_alex: mitigation step 1: isolate node — cordon gpu-node-12, drain non-critical pods. Step 2: restart collector-daemon and nccl-health-checker on remaining nodes to force clean rendezvous

maggie: rolling restart of serving pods in the affected pool started, will keep 1 replica live for canary traffic, routing policy set to fallback-model-v2 for latency-sensitive customers :warning:

eli: temporarily lower per-request max-seq to 1024 via runtime-config to reduce KV cache pressure for live traffic (applied to route group `prod-tp4`)

dev-platform: applied cordon, drain in progress. Notifying infra to check NIC error counters (possible IB/NVLink flaps)

incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by sre_alex (15:03:27 UTC) — incident severity: Sev2.

maggie: customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased latencies and transient 5xxs affecting multi-GPU inference. Root cause appears to be GPU node flaps triggering NCCL rendezvous failures; we've isolated the node and applied mitigations. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Approve?

eli: approve. Add note that we've set automatic fallback to single-GPU model variants for critical customers

oncall-next: taking handoff in 15 minutes. leave runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-rendezvous — next steps: if restarts don't stabilize, consider scaling Dedicated pools and enabling per-tenant isolation for high-seq jobs

sre_alex: current status: drains at 15:05:40 UTC, canary route healthy, error rate down from 8% -> 1.2% on fallback routes. Will monitor for 10m, then uncordon after NIC/verifications.

maggie: added tags to incident ticket and flagged customers for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Handoff note created, next oncall: oncall-next, handoff ETA 15:20 UTC.
